# Swarm core doctrine — draft 0

*The rules every one of meshe's swarms holds in common, with the reason attached to each, so a new project can start from them instead of re-deriving them. Distilled 2026-09-09 from four doctrines by sentence-level diff (swarm-builder F-009): the dashboard (`docs/swarm.md`, ratified 2026-07-17), the workstation (`~/vault/Rebuild/Swarm.md`, 2026-07-20), leadworks-saas (`CLAUDE.md` + `orchestrator.md`, v3), and the forms parity loop (`PARITY_LOOP.md`). A rule is **core** when all four hold it or meshe ratifies it, **usual** when three do; anything held by fewer is a project setting and is listed at the end as an option, not a rule. Draft: nothing here is ratified; swarm-builder exploration 03 holds the open questions and D-entries will ratify it piece by piece.*

*A rule without its reason gets optimized away by whoever thinks they know better (dashboard `d64c042`, 2026-08-17). Every rule below carries its reason.*

---

## 1. Shape

A swarm is an **orchestrator** in the main loop, a set of **gate roles** that judge and cannot fix, and a set of **engineer roles** that build and cannot judge their own work, all reading one **canon** document and working to one **pinned contract**. The gate roles and the playbooks are the same in every project. The engineers, the contract's content, the deploy classes and the checklists are the project's.

| Layer | Owned by | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Core | this doctrine | rules below; gate-role method; playbooks; contract template; output contracts; cost ledger |
| Project | the repo's `docs/swarm.md` project section | engineer roles and their stacks; test commands and tiers; deploy classes and the HELD list; single-writer resources; verifier and qa checklists; model assignment; snapshot vs contract |

## 2. Core rules (held by all four swarms)

**C-1 — The canon is a document; agent files are thin wiring.**
Every agent's first action is to read the canon (`docs/swarm.md`) and the repo `CLAUDE.md`; its own file only names its tools, model and return shape.
*Why:* a rule that lives in one agent's prompt is invisible to the others and to meshe; a rule in the canon binds every role and can be diffed, versioned and synced. (dashboard `swarm.md:3-4`, workstation `Swarm.md:8-9`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:3-5`, forms `parity-loop.md:5`)

**C-2 — The orchestrator writes no production code. Fixing inline is a logged exception after a stuck trip, never a habit.**
*Why:* the orchestrator holds the whole context and the whole authority; if it also writes, nothing independent checks it, and its context fills with code instead of state. In the forms loop it never fixes at all — the failure goes to a fresh process. (dashboard `swarm.md:11`, workstation `Swarm.md:77`, leadworks `orchestrator.md:28`, forms `parity-loop.md:6`)

**C-3 — A gate cannot fix what it judges. Enforce it with tool grants, not instructions.**
The verifier has no Edit/Write. The test-writer has no Bash. The adjudicator has no Write. A gate that could quietly become the author will.
*Why:* 2026-08-24, dashboard: roles emulated from a session rooted in the wrong directory had full tools and were "held only by instruction"; the doctrine held, the enforcement didn't, and meshe did not notice until after deploy (dashboard D-033). Leadworks' 13 roles all hold Write/Edit/Bash and its separation is prompt-only — the one swarm where this rule is a wish. (dashboard `swarm.md:15`, workstation `Swarm.md:31`, forms `PARITY_LOOP.md:77-78`)

**C-4 — Stuck is three identical failures with zero progress. Then stop that line, record attempts and hypotheses, route around, surface to meshe.**
Progress = a different error, a new file, red→green. Reset the count on progress. Siblings keep going; only true dependents wait.
*Why:* looping on one wall burns the budget and hides the wall; a `BLOCKED:` block with exact command, error, attempts and competing hypotheses is a thirty-second decision for meshe. Written independently in near-identical words by three swarms; the forms loop's `THRASH_LIMIT=3` is the same rule mechanised. (dashboard `swarm.md:141-143`, workstation `Swarm.md:74`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:30-31`, forms `loop.sh:95-100`)

**C-5 — Model policy by role: judgment runs on the strongest model, implementation on the workhorse, retrieval on the cheapest.**
The shape is core; the assignment is the project's (the dashboard verifier is Fable and its engineers Opus; the workstation scout is Haiku; the forms adjudicator is Fable and its builder Opus).
*Why (leadworks v3 retro):* "a stronger model's wins concentrate in judgment … while implementation under a locked spec is Opus-shaped work." A pushed secret or a wrong verdict is forever; a wrong line of code is a red test. (dashboard `swarm.md:11-15`, workstation `Swarm.md:34-38`, leadworks `orchestrator.md:32-33`, forms `PARITY_LOOP.md:93-94`)

**C-6 — Every dispatch names what it may touch. Single-writer resources are partitioned, never shared.**
The orchestrator partitions ownership into disjoint file lists per track before dispatching; the project lists its single-writer resources (schema, router registration, README/CHANGELOG, the test DB, migration order) and assigns each to exactly one dispatch.
*Why:* two writers on one tree or DB cross-truncate, cross-merge and cross-blame (dashboard issues #4/#7, 2026-07-18; leadworks migration/FK order). (dashboard `swarm.md:149-154`, workstation `Swarm.md:65`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:23-24`, forms disjoint ownership)

**C-7 — Escalation is a structured decision, never a guess.**
`DECISION NEEDED — <one line>` / `A) …` / `B) …` / `Recommendation: <A|B> — <one clause>`. A judgment call (appearance, scope, anything altering a locked pattern) stops the line and goes to meshe with options; the ruling is logged so the same question never escalates twice.
*Why:* an agent that invents an answer to a taste question ships the wrong thing confidently; an agent that asks without options costs meshe the analysis she delegated. (dashboard `swarm.md:61-65`, workstation `Swarm.md:85-92`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:70`, forms `PARITY_LOOP.md:262`)

**C-8 — Never weaken the oracle to get green.**
Engineers never edit tests; a suspected-wrong test is a flag in the return and the verifier rules. A normalizer, allow-list or tolerance is loosened only with meshe's explicit sign-off. "The urge to loosen is the signal to stop."
*Why:* a test edited to pass proves nothing and hides the bug it was written for; the forms loop's gates went 28→4 flags only because the target could not move. (dashboard `swarm.md:131`, workstation `Swarm.md:31`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:123`, forms `PARITY_LOOP.md:55-57, 267-268`)

**C-9 — An unsatisfiable contract requirement is a blocker: park it, keep working, surface it. Never amend the contract, never decide, never stop and wait.** *(Ratified by meshe 2026-09-09 17:03 PDT, swarm-builder D-006 — the first rule ratified rather than distilled.)*
When a requirement cannot be met as written (a pinned value the environment contradicts, a row two facts make impossible), the run records `BLOCKED:` for that requirement — exact evidence, what was tried, the options with a recommendation — parks it and everything that depends on it, and continues every line that does not. The run finishes with the blocker at the top of its report (and on the issue, labelled `blocked`/`needs-meshe`). It does not rewrite the row, choose an option, or write a D-entry; provisional choices are O-rows.
*Why (meshe):* "Unsatisfiable contract requirements should become blockers and should bubble up to me" and "if the swarm is able to continue work on other tasks when it encounters a blocker it should. I frequently run swarms overnight or while I'm not at a computer and if the swarm stops and waits for me it's going to invalidate the token cache costing me money." First-run evidence: swarm-builder F-014 — the orchestrator chose a clock label itself and logged it as a decision.

## 3. Usual rules (held by three of four; a project opts out with a reason in its section)

**U-1 — The contract is pinned and pasted verbatim into every dispatch. Canon is never paraphrased into a dispatch; agents read it themselves.**
*Why:* a paraphrase drifts a little each hop; by the third relay the engineer is building to the orchestrator's memory of the plan. (dashboard `swarm.md:26-27`, workstation `Swarm.md:64-68`, forms `parity-loop.md:34-35`; leadworks names its input docs but has no verbatim rule)

**U-2 — Docs land in the same dispatch as the change.**
The engineer that changes behaviour updates the README, CHANGELOG, vault note or cheatsheet in the same return; the orchestrator assigns shared docs to exactly one dispatch. *Why:* a docs pass "later" is a docs pass never; drift makes the rebuild artifacts lie. (dashboard `swarm.md:17-19`, workstation `Swarm.md:29`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:98-100`)

**U-3 — Deterministic gates run with zero agent tokens.**
An issue sweep, a harness run, a lock check, a drift audit is a script, not a Claude session; a model is spawned only when the script finds something for it to do. *Why:* zero eligible issues = zero tokens (dashboard `swarm.md:37-39`); the forms harness runs with no agent and hands one failure to one model (forms `loop.sh:7`). (workstation `Swarm.md:103`)

**U-4 — Findings are evidence, not argument: a failing test where practical, a command and its output otherwise.**
*Why:* a finding expressed as a test is red-first by construction and becomes a permanent guard; a finding expressed as prose is re-litigated. (dashboard `swarm.md:161-162`, workstation `Swarm.md:93`, leadworks `CLAUDE.md:94`)

## 4. Contract shape

Every build runs to a **pinned contract** the orchestrator distils from the approved plan (or the issue) before any dispatch. It carries:

1. **Surface** — routes and JSON shapes, function signatures, constants, table DDL, tool names and docstrings; or, for a snapshot build, the frozen target and its provenance.
2. **Rejections table** — `| input shape | status | message |`, one row for every required field, every one-of group, every bound, every NOT NULL column of every new or changed table. The test-writer writes one test per row; the verifier cross-checks the rows against the DDL and the bodies. *Why:* dashboard #20 → #21 (2026-09-07): a rule stated in prose ("items → what required") had no row, so no test, so no implementation, so a 500 in production behind 2,207 green tests. "A rule enforced by no test doesn't exist."
3. **Definition of Done** — which test tiers must be green, what the live probe must show, what the deploy class is, which docs must move.
4. **HELD list** — what this build may never do without meshe (deploy to production, destructive schema, outbound send, money, deletion, secrets).
5. **Ownership** — the disjoint file lists per track and the single-writer assignments (C-6).

## 5. Gate roles (core method; the project supplies the checklist)

| Role | Tools | Method |
|---|---|---|
| `swarm-verifier` | Read, Bash, Grep, Glob — **no Edit/Write** | Fresh context. Reads canon + contract + affected-test paths. Confirms new tests failed for the right reason. Runs affected tests, then the full suite only after those pass, then e2e only if the project says so. Adversarial diff review against the project checklist. Names the deploy class the diff falls in. Verdict: first line exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`; then numbered `file — problem — fix hint — severity`; then what ran, durations, anything for meshe. Never spawns background watcher shells (two `while pgrep` loops deadlocked on each other, dashboard 2026-07-17). |
| `swarm-test-writer` | Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob — **no Bash** | Fresh context. Writes RED tests from the contract surface and the Rejections table, in the tier the project's test map names, touching only its ownership list, following neighbouring tests' style. Desk-checks imports and fixtures because it cannot run. Returns files written, affected-test paths, and every contract ambiguity as a flag, never a resolution. |
| `swarm-qa` | Read, Bash, Grep, Glob — **no Edit/Write** | The consumer's view. Dispatched with **no contract and no plan**: only the surface (OpenAPI, tool docstrings, a base URL of the *test* app) and "use this the way a client, a script and a tired human would". Drives realistic shapes (omitted optionals, blanks, unicode, boundaries, retries) and reads what comes back. Returns `VERDICT: CLEAN|FINDINGS` with each finding as a pasted failing test. *Why:* everyone else who tested #20 held the contract; the seam was found in two calls by someone who didn't (dashboard #21 D). |
| `swarm-security` | Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, web — **no Edit/Write** | Reads the code like an attacker against the project's threat model. A confirmed critical finding blocks a green gate. Findings as failing exploit tests. Runs at every wave gate and before anything irreversible. |
| `swarm-scout` | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash (read-only) | Recon that never re-derives the system: canon → relevant note → file. `FACTS: / PATHS: / STATE: / GAPS:` in ≤10 lines. Cheapest model. |
| `swarm-researcher` | web, Read, Grep — no Bash, no Edit/Write | Check-the-web-before-naming-a-cause as a visible hop. `CANDIDATES:` with URL and confidence; `NO-SOURCE:` for labelled hypotheses. |

Engineers are project roles: one per track (backend, frontend, port, migration…), full tools inside their ownership list, scoped test runs only, docs in-dispatch, never editing tests (C-8).

## 6. Playbooks

**P-A — Build to a contract** (dashboard `/swarm-build`, generalised): preconditions (branch, clean tree, no stray suites, `swarm-working` marker if an issue tracks the build) → pin the contract (§4) → partition ownership (C-6) → dispatch test-writers in parallel → confirm red → dispatch engineers per track as their tests exist → stuck-detector (C-4) → verifier → (qa when a route or tool surface changed) → commit on green in logical units → deploy per class → close the loop (docs, vault, memory, report).

**P-B — Build to a frozen snapshot** (forms `loop.sh`, generalised — swarm-builder F-009 T-8): a deterministic harness compares the built artifact and a frozen target through the same corpus with the same stubs and writes `report.json` (status, one severity-ordered `active_failure`, `needs_adjudication`, ordered failures, coverage). A bounded shell driver runs it with no agent; on red it spawns a judgment model only when adjudication is flagged, then an implementation model with exactly one failure, verbatim; commits every iteration; stops on the thrash limit. The frozen target has a provenance file; the harness self-tests against itself before the loop; the normalizer is an explicit allow-list; every non-first-party request is stubbed or loud-red; divergence is a bug in the new artifact by definition. A new domain supplies: target + provenance, corpus + inventory extractor, gates with severities, an adapter, the allow-list, stubs, two role prompts, config.

**P-C — Fix one issue** (dashboard `/fix-it`, generalised): there is always an issue (create one for a described bug) → triage bucket first: clear defect / judgment (stop, options, `needs-meshe`) / can't repro (ask) → red-first regression test → minimal fix, scoped runs → gate (verifier; qa if a surface changed) → deploy per class → escalate on stuck → terminal comment with root cause, files, test, SHA, probe evidence and the cost footer.

## 7. Output contracts

Plain text by default: what / files / affected-test paths / scoped-run tail / flags, ≤10–15 lines per role. *Why:* structured-output schemas caused retry-cap kills of agents whose work had already landed (dashboard test-rule 6). Where two *processes* talk through a file (P-B), the file is machine JSON and the agent's own reply is one strict line. Verdicts always start with `VERDICT:`.

## 8. Deploy classes (shape; the project fills the lists)

**Auto** — code-only and additive schema; gate = red-first test + affected + full suite green (+ e2e if the project says); then apply → build → restart → **timed, read-only live probe** → watchdog. *Why:* a 200 is not evidence; `/api/comms/owed` sat at 9.1 s for months behind a green suite. Never fire a write at production to time it — a team once mass-deleted "testing all the endpoints".
**Rollback** — probe fails or a new alert inside the window → revert + restart + label + evidence.
**Held** — never auto, regardless of green: the project's HELD list (§4.4) plus anything remote with no rollback script. Lands as a branch with the exact deploy commands stated.

## 9. Observability (core tooling; one copy)

- **Cost footer** on every terminal comment: per-model tokens and sticker-price estimate from the session's transcripts (dashboard `session_cost.py`, leadworks `session-cost.mjs` — same table, one should survive).
- **Role ledger**: the same transcripts keyed by `agentType` from `subagents/*.meta.json` give dispatches, turns, tokens and cost per role (swarm-builder F-002, F-010: the main loop was 49% and 82% of two sessions — relay is where usage goes).
- **Event ledger at zero tokens**: `SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` / per-tool hooks carry `agent_id`, `agent_type` and the transcript path (swarm-builder F-007); a plugin-carried hook writes start, every tool call, stop, for every role in every project.

## 10. How this doctrine changes

A post-mortem names each deliverable **core** or **project** (dashboard #21: A/B project, C/D/E core). Core items become an issue on `meshe-dev/swarm-builder` before the project fix ships; a core change carries its rationale, a regression case, a version bump, and a line in each consuming project's log when it updates. *Why:* fifteen dashboard swarm commits each fixed a real pathology and none reached another swarm (swarm-builder F-006); the improvement loop is this paragraph or it is nothing.

## 11. Project settings (held by fewer than three; each project chooses and records why)

- **Push**: leadworks never pushes without the human; the dashboard auto-deploys the auto lane; the workstation orchestrator commits and pushes. Record the choice.
- **Return channel**: plain text (three) vs machine JSON between processes (forms).
- **Salvage before re-dispatch**: check the working tree and the live state before re-running — the work often landed (dashboard, workstation). Recommended wherever an agent can die mid-write.
- **Headless lane**: a deterministic sweep spawning `claude -p` on a label (dashboard) vs interactive-only by ruling (workstation) vs none (leadworks).
- **Cost footer on issues** (dashboard, leadworks fix-it) — recommended everywhere the ledger exists.
- **Environment canary** before believing measurements (dashboard).
- **Perturbation demonstration** on every gate: corrupt → RED → revert (leadworks).
- **Context checkpoint** every N iterations with state files as the whole resume state (forms).

## 12. What a project section must supply (the `/swarm-init` questionnaire — derive first, ask last)

| Item | Derive from | Ask only if |
|---|---|---|
| Stack, test framework, test command(s), tiers | repo (manifests, CI, existing tests, README) | no tests exist — then the first contract creates the tier |
| Engineer roles and ownership tracks | repo layout (backend/frontend/… directories) | tracks are ambiguous |
| Single-writer resources | repo (schema, router registration, README/CHANGELOG, lockfiles, migrations) | — |
| Deploy: units, build, restart, probe URL | repo (compose, systemd, deploy scripts), the vault | the production host is not recorded anywhere |
| HELD list | §8 defaults + anything remote, destructive, outbound, money, secrets | the project has a class the defaults miss |
| Model assignment | C-5 shape + the project's judgment/implementation split | — |
| Contract vs snapshot | is there a frozen reference artifact? | both apply |
| Headless lane | default none | meshe wants a watcher |
| Push policy | default never without meshe | — |
| Verifier / qa / security checklists | the project's locked patterns in `CLAUDE.md` | — |
